title: Verified database backups and their purge
summary: Backs a Firebird database up through the service API, restores it into a temporary database to prove it, lists and purges only its own files
intro: Read this when you are about to change a Firebird database, or when old backups fill the disk. drag-lint repo backup --connection makes a backup without gbak.exe, restores it into a temporary database and compares it; repo alter-table --apply does the same by itself. repo backup list and repo backup purge look only at the backups drag-lint made.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint repo backup --connection "<Firebird connection string>" [--verify <full|quick>] [--table <T>] [--backup-dir <folder>] [--backup-name <name>] [--project <project file>] [--json]
help: drag-lint repo backup         --connection "<Firebird connection string>" [--verify <full|quick>] [--table <T>] [--backup-dir <folder>] [--backup-name <name>] [--project <project file>] [--json]   (a backup of the DATABASE through the Firebird service API, as DLFR_BACKUP_<database>_<yyyymmdd>_<hhnnss>.fbk unless --backup-name gives the name (a name not a path, .fbk added, an existing file is never overwritten); restored into a temporary database and compared unless --verify quick; free space checked first; a server on ANOTHER machine is allowed with --verify quick given explicitly: it writes the file on its own disk, the host and that path are printed and recorded as NOT verified (remote, not verified), the free space is not checked, --backup-name is refused there (exit 1 before connecting: the automatic time-stamped name is used so nothing is overwritten), and purge never deletes it; recorded in %LOCALAPPDATA%\drag-lint\db-backups.json)

drag-lint repo backup         list [--connection <..>] [--json] | purge --keep <N> [--connection <..> [--apply]] [--dry-run] [--json]   (the recorded backups; purge is a dry run without --apply and deletes only backups of the database --connection opens, only recorded files whose size and date did not change, and never the newest or the newest verified one)

questions.ask: How do I make a Firebird backup that is proven to restore?
Which database backups did drag-lint make, and how much space do they take?
How do I delete old database backups safely?
